category: Geometry II: primitives, curves, operations, virtual operations, CAD import & LiveLink
description: The geometry features not covered in the first Geometry chunk: point/line/curve primitives, the remaining 2D and 3D solids, Loft, Intersection, Compose, Chamfer, conversions, Form Assembly, Scale/Copy/Split/Thicken, mesh-control entities, parts and part libraries, the virtual operations (Ignore Edges/Vertices, Form Composite Faces, Collapse Edges, Remove Details), CAD Import Module repair and defeaturing, LiveLink for CAD, cumulative selections, measuring and export. All features are created with model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create(tag, type), configured with feature(tag).set(...) and built with geom("geom1").run() (Build All).

tools.name: Point
tools.description: Geometry primitive that creates one or more isolated points (vertices) from a coordinate list or expressions. Points are needed for point loads/sources, point probes, mesh size control at a location, and as vertices for later Line Segment or Interpolation Curve features.
tools.usage: Geometry > More Primitives > Point (pt1); API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("pt1", "Point")

parameters.name: p
parameters.description: Coordinates as a sdim x N array (one column per point); expressions with parameters are allowed.

parameters.name: workplane
parameters.description: In 3D, optionally define the point in a work plane.

parameters.name: selresult
parameters.description: Create a selection of the resulting point(s) for use in physics.

tools.notes: A point inside a domain becomes part of that domain's boundary structure only after Form Union; in an assembly it stays a separate object. Points on curved faces are projected onto the face only if you use the Point on a work plane or the Partition Edges feature.

tools.name: Line Segment
tools.description: Creates a straight edge between two points given as coordinates or as existing vertices. Used for beam/truss/pipe elements, edge loads, current-carrying wires (edge currents in Magnetic Fields), cut lines that must exist in the geometry, and as sketches for later extrusion.
tools.usage: Geometry > More Primitives > Line Segment (ls1); API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("ls1", "LineSegment")

parameters.name: specify1 / specify2
parameters.description: coord | vertex - how each endpoint is given.

parameters.name: coord1 / coord2
parameters.description: Endpoint coordinates when specified by coordinates.

parameters.name: selection("vertex1") / selection("vertex2")
parameters.description: Existing vertices when specified by vertex.

tools.notes: Polygon builds a chain of segments in one feature; Bezier Polygon adds curved segments.

tools.name: Bezier Polygon
tools.description: Creates a curve (open, closed or as a solid in 2D) from a sequence of linear, quadratic and cubic Bezier segments with control points and weights. It is the general sketch tool for airfoils, cam profiles, fillet-like curves and any shape you can describe by control points, and the feature the GUI's Sketch tools write to.
tools.usage: Geometry > More Primitives > Bezier Polygon (b1); API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("b1", "BezierPolygon")

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: solid | closed | open curve (solid only in 2D or work planes).

parameters.name: degree
parameters.description: Array with the degree (1, 2 or 3) of each segment.

parameters.name: p
parameters.description: Control point coordinates for all segments, consecutive segments sharing endpoints.

parameters.name: w
parameters.description: Weights per control point (rational Bezier), e.g. 1/sqrt(2) middle weight for a circular arc.

tools.notes: Control points are listed per segment in p, so shared endpoints appear once; the number of weights equals the total number of control points including repeats (degree+1 per segment). Since 6.0 the GUI also offers Quadratic Bezier and Cubic Bezier as separate features.

tools.name: Parametric Curve
tools.description: Creates a curve from coordinate expressions in a parameter s over an interval, e.g. x = R*cos(s), y = R*sin(s), z = p*s/(2*pi) for a helix path or a spline written as a formula. The result can be used for sweeping profiles, as an edge for loads, or as the boundary of a 2D domain when combined with Convert to Solid.
tools.usage: Geometry > More Primitives > Parametric Curve (pc1); API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("pc1", "ParametricCurve")

parameters.name: parname
parameters.description: Parameter name (default s).

parameters.name: parmin / parmax
parameters.description: Parameter interval.

parameters.name: coord
parameters.description: x, y (and z) expressions in the parameter and in global parameters/functions.

parameters.name: rtol / maxknots
parameters.description: Relative tolerance and maximum number of knots for the internal spline fit.

tools.notes: Expressions may call global functions (Interpolation, Analytic), so tabulated profiles can be made smooth. Parametric Surface is the 2-parameter analogue.

tools.name: Parametric Surface
tools.description: Creates a 3D surface from x, y, z expressions in two parameters (s1, s2) over a rectangular parameter domain: terrain from an Elevation function, lens surfaces, corrugated sheets, mathematically defined mirrors. The surface can then be thickened, used to partition solids, or closed into a solid with Convert to Solid.
tools.usage: Geometry > More Primitives > Parametric Surface (ps1); API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("ps1", "ParametricSurface")

parameters.name: parname1 / parname2
parameters.description: Parameter names (s1, s2).

parameters.name: parmin1/parmax1, parmin2/parmax2
parameters.description: Parameter ranges.

parameters.name: coord
parameters.description: x, y, z expressions.

parameters.name: rtol / maxknots
parameters.description: Approximation tolerance and knot limit of the internal B-spline fit.

tools.notes: Very wiggly surfaces need a smaller rtol and more knots and become slow; downsample the underlying data first. Use Thicken to give a parametric surface a finite thickness.

tools.name: Interpolation Curve
tools.description: Creates an open, closed or solid curve that interpolates (or with a tolerance, approximates) a list of data points given in a table, a file or coordinate vectors. This is how digitised profiles (measured airfoil coordinates, traced outlines from images, coastlines) become geometry; optional start/end tangent or zero-curvature conditions control the ends.
tools.usage: Geometry > More Primitives > Interpolation Curve (ic1); API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("ic1", "InterpolationCurve")

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: table | file | vectors.

parameters.name: table / filename / x,y,z
parameters.description: The data points (N x sdim) depending on source.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: open | closed | solid.

parameters.name: rtol
parameters.description: Relative tolerance; 0 forces exact interpolation, >0 gives a smoother approximating spline.

parameters.name: startcond / endcond
parameters.description: none | zerocurv | tangent end conditions with starttang/endtang vectors.

tools.notes: Data files can be sectionwise or spreadsheet format; use importData() to embed the file. Noisy data with rtol = 0 produces oscillating curves - set a tolerance instead.

tools.name: Ellipse
tools.description: 2D primitive (also usable in 3D work planes) creating a solid or curve ellipse from semi-axes, centre, rotation angle and optionally an angular sector and concentric layers. Used for elliptical waveguides, lens cross-sections and elliptical inclusions.
tools.usage: Geometry > Ellipse (e1); API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("e1", "Ellipse")

parameters.name: semiaxes
parameters.description: a and b semi-axis lengths.

parameters.name: pos / rot
parameters.description: Centre and rotation angle in degrees.

parameters.name: angle
parameters.description: Sector angle (360 for a full ellipse).

parameters.name: type / layer
parameters.description: solid | curve and optional layer thicknesses.

tools.notes: Ellipsoid is the 3D counterpart. Circle covers the special case with layers and sector options as well.

tools.name: Square
tools.description: 2D primitive creating a square (solid or curve) of given side, position, rotation and optional layers, a shortcut for Rectangle with equal sides. Common for unit cells, periodic metamaterial cells and test domains.
tools.usage: Geometry > Square (sq1); API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("sq1", "Square")

parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Side length.

parameters.name: pos / base
parameters.description: Position and whether it refers to the corner or the centre.

parameters.name: rot
parameters.description: Rotation angle.

parameters.name: layer / layername
parameters.description: Layers inward from selected sides.

tools.notes: Rectangle exposes independent width and height; both share the layer mechanism used to create PML or boundary-layer domains.

tools.name: Hexahedron
tools.description: 3D primitive defined by its eight corner vertices, which need not form a box, so skewed or tapered brick-like solids (wedges, sheared cells, tapered fins) can be created without Boolean operations. The faces are bilinear surfaces through the corners.
tools.usage: Geometry > More Primitives > Hexahedron (hex1); API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("hex1", "Hexahedron")

parameters.name: p
parameters.description: 3 x 8 array of corner coordinates in the documented vertex order.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: solid | surface.

tools.notes: Pyramid and Tetrahedron are the other vertex-defined primitives; Block is the axis-aligned special case with layers.

tools.name: Pyramid
tools.description: 3D primitive creating a (truncated) pyramid with rectangular base from base sizes, height, top-to-base ratio and displacements of the top face, plus position, axis and rotation. Useful for horn antennas, pyramidal absorbers, funnels and tapered dies.
tools.usage: Geometry > More Primitives > Pyramid (pyr1); API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("pyr1", "Pyramid")

parameters.name: basesize
parameters.description: Base side lengths.

parameters.name: h
parameters.description: Height.

parameters.name: ratio
parameters.description: Top-to-base size ratio (0 for an apex).

parameters.name: displ
parameters.description: Lateral displacement of the top face.

parameters.name: pos / axis / rot
parameters.description: Placement.

tools.notes: Cone is the circular-base analogue.

tools.name: Ellipsoid
tools.description: 3D primitive creating a solid or surface ellipsoid from three semi-axes, centre, axis orientation, rotation and optional concentric layers. Used for cells and particles in bio-models, inclusions in composites and elliptical reflectors.
tools.usage: Geometry > More Primitives > Ellipsoid (elp1); API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("elp1", "Ellipsoid")

parameters.name: semiaxes
parameters.description: a, b, c semi-axes.

parameters.name: pos / axistype / rot
parameters.description: Centre and orientation.

parameters.name: layer
parameters.description: Layer thicknesses for concentric shells.

tools.notes: Sphere is the special case with equal semi-axes and is preferred when available because its faces are exact.

tools.name: Helix
tools.description: 3D primitive that creates a solid, surface or curve helix (coil) of circular cross-section from number of turns, major and minor radii, axial pitch, chirality and optional end taper. It is the fastest way to model solenoid windings, springs, helical antennas and stents without sweeping a circle along a parametric curve.
tools.usage: Geometry > More Primitives > Helix (hel1); API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("hel1", "Helix")

parameters.name: turns
parameters.description: Number of turns (may be fractional).

parameters.name: rmaj / rmin
parameters.description: Major (helix) radius and minor (wire) radius.

parameters.name: axialpitch
parameters.description: Axial distance per turn; radial pitch for conical/spiral coils.

parameters.name: chirality
parameters.description: right | left.

parameters.name: endcaps
parameters.description: Flat or perpendicular end caps; type solid | surface | curve.

tools.notes: Many turns give many faces and a heavy mesh; for inductance calculations the homogenised Coil feature on a simple cylinder is usually preferable.

tools.name: Loft
tools.description: Creates a solid or surface by lofting (skinning) through a sequence of profile curves or faces, optionally with guide curves and start/end tangency conditions. It builds transitions between different cross-sections - ducts changing from round to square, blades, hulls, nozzles - that Extrude and Sweep cannot represent.
tools.usage: Geometry > Loft (loft1); API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("loft1", "Loft")

parameters.name: Profile objects / edges
parameters.description: Ordered list of closed profile curves (or faces) to loft through.

parameters.name: Guide curves
parameters.description: Optional edges the loft must follow.

parameters.name: Start/End profile condition
parameters.description: Free, normal, or tangent to a face.

parameters.name: Aligned vertices
parameters.description: Vertex pairs to control twist between profiles.

tools.notes: Requires the Design Module (Loft, 3D Chamfer/Fillet, Thicken, Midsurface and Detect Interferences are Design Module features). Profiles should have the same number of edges or specify aligned vertices to avoid twisted surfaces.

tools.name: Intersection (geometry)
tools.description: Boolean operation returning the common volume (or area) of the input objects, optionally keeping the input objects and interior boundaries. Used to trim a shape to a bounding region - e.g. intersect an imported cable with a sector wedge to model one periodic sector - or to extract the overlap of two bodies.
tools.usage: Geometry > Booleans and Partitions > Intersection (int1); API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("int1", "Intersection")

parameters.name: selection("input")
parameters.description: Objects to intersect.

parameters.name: intbnd
parameters.description: Keep interior boundaries (on/off).

parameters.name: keep
parameters.description: Keep input objects.

tools.notes: Compose expresses arbitrary set formulas; Partition Objects/Domains keep both sides. Intersecting curve objects with solids gives the trimmed curve.

tools.name: Compose
tools.description: Generalised Boolean operation that combines several objects according to a set formula using object names and the operators + (union), * (intersection) and - (difference) with parentheses, e.g. (blk1+cyl1)-sph1. One Compose node replaces a chain of Union/Difference/Intersection nodes and keeps the sequence readable.
tools.usage: Geometry > Booleans and Partitions > Compose (co1); API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("co1", "Compose")

parameters.name: formula
parameters.description: Set formula in object names.

parameters.name: selection("input")
parameters.description: Objects referenced by the formula.

parameters.name: intbnd / keep / repairtol
parameters.description: Interior boundaries, keep inputs, repair tolerance.

tools.notes: Objects created by array features are named like arr1(1,2); quote nothing - names are used bare in the formula.

tools.name: Chamfer
tools.description: Replaces selected vertices (2D) or edges (3D, Design Module) with a flat bevel of given distance(s), the planar counterpart of Fillet. Chamfers are used to remove singular corners that cause stress or field concentrations and to reproduce machined edges from drawings.
tools.usage: Geometry > Chamfer (cha1); API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("cha1", "Chamfer")

parameters.name: selection("point") / selection("edge")
parameters.description: Vertices (2D) or edges (3D) to chamfer.

parameters.name: dist
parameters.description: Chamfer distance; dist1/dist2 for asymmetric chamfers in 3D.

tools.notes: 3D chamfers and fillets on edges need the Design Module (CAD kernel); without it, chamfer the 2D sketch before extruding.

tools.name: Delete Entities
tools.description: Removes selected objects, domains, boundaries, edges or vertices from the geometry sequence output. Deleting a domain from a solid turns the remaining faces into a surface object; deleting faces opens a solid. Commonly used after CAD import to drop screws, small parts or the surrounding assembly components that are irrelevant to the analysis.
tools.usage: Geometry > Delete Entities (del1); API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("del1", "Delete")

parameters.name: selection("input")
parameters.description: Entities to delete, specified by object name and entity level via .init(dim).

parameters.name: Geometric entity level
parameters.description: object | domain | boundary | edge | point.

tools.notes: Deleting is destructive for the downstream sequence; for optional parts prefer disabling features or use selections plus Delete after Form Union. Delete Fillets/Delete Holes (CAD Import Module) remove features rather than entities.

tools.name: Convert to Solid
tools.description: Unites the selected objects and converts them into a single solid object: closed surface or curve objects become filled solids, and several solids become one object with interior boundaries. Used after importing STL/mesh surfaces, after building an enclosure from parametric or lofted surfaces, and to turn a closed 2D curve into a domain.
tools.usage: Geometry > Conversions > Convert to Solid (csol1); API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("csol1", "ConvertToSolid")

parameters.name: selection("input")
parameters.description: Objects to convert; surfaces must form closed shells.

parameters.name: keep
parameters.description: Keep the input objects.

parameters.name: repairtol
parameters.description: Tolerance used to close small gaps.

tools.notes: If the shell is not watertight the result stays a surface; check with Measure (object type) and raise repairtol or fix the gap. Convert to Surface and Convert to Curve go the other way.

tools.name: Convert to Surface
tools.description: Converts solid, surface or curve objects into a single surface object made of the boundaries of the inputs, discarding the volumes. Used to extract the skin of a solid for shell/membrane analysis, to keep only the walls of a CAD enclosure, or to make a surface for Thicken.
tools.usage: Geometry > Conversions > Convert to Surface (csur1); API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("csur1", "ConvertToSurface")

parameters.name: selection("input")
parameters.description: Objects to convert.

parameters.name: keep
parameters.description: Keep inputs.

tools.notes: Shell interfaces can work directly on faces of solids (using a face selection), so conversion is only needed when the solid should disappear. Midsurface (Design Module) creates a surface midway between opposite faces instead.

tools.name: Convert to Curve
tools.description: Converts objects into a curve object consisting of their edges, dropping faces and volumes. Used to obtain a wire frame for beam/truss/pipe models from a solid CAD part, for edge currents or to keep an outline as a sketch.
tools.usage: Geometry > Conversions > Convert to Curve (ccur1); API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("ccur1", "ConvertToCurve")

parameters.name: selection("input")
parameters.description: Objects to convert.

parameters.name: keep
parameters.description: Keep inputs.

tools.notes: Convert to Point exists as well (vertices only).

tools.name: Form Assembly
tools.description: Alternative action of the final geometry node (Form Union/Assembly, tag fin): instead of merging all objects into one with shared boundaries, it keeps each object separate and creates identity or contact pairs where objects touch. Required for structural contact, sliding/rotating interfaces (rotating machinery), non-conforming meshes across parts, and imprinting-free assemblies from CAD; the price is pair constraints instead of a conforming mesh.
tools.usage: Geometry > Form Union/Assembly (fin) > Action: Form an assembly; API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").feature("fin").set("action", "assembly")

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: union | assembly.

parameters.name: createpairs
parameters.description: Create identity pairs on coincident faces.

parameters.name: pairtype
parameters.description: identity | contact for the automatically created pairs.

parameters.name: imprint
parameters.description: Imprint touching faces so that boundaries match on both sides (recommended when meshes should be similar).

parameters.name: repairtol
parameters.description: Tolerance for detecting touching faces.

tools.notes: With an assembly the physics interfaces need pair features (Continuity, Thermal Contact, Fluid-Fluid Interface, Contact) to couple the parts; without them the parts are insulated from each other. Form Union remains the default and best choice whenever a conforming mesh is possible.

tools.name: Scale
tools.description: Transform feature that scales selected objects isotropically or by different factors per axis about a chosen point. Typical uses: convert an import in wrong units (mm read as m), squash a model to unit thickness, or generate a family of similar shapes in a sweep.
tools.usage: Geometry > Transforms > Scale (sca1); API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("sca1", "Scale")

parameters.name: selection("input")
parameters.description: Objects to scale.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: isotropic | anisotropic.

parameters.name: factor
parameters.description: Scale factor (or three factors).

parameters.name: pos
parameters.description: Centre of scaling.

parameters.name: keep
parameters.description: Keep the original objects.

tools.notes: For unit mistakes on import it is cleaner to set the Length unit of the Import feature or of the geometry (geom1.lengthUnit("mm")).

tools.name: Copy (geometry)
tools.description: Transform feature that creates one or more displaced copies of the selected objects along a displacement vector, keeping the originals. Simpler than Array when only a few copies at arbitrary offsets are required, e.g. duplicating an electrode to make a pair.
tools.usage: Geometry > Transforms > Copy (copy1); API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("copy1", "Copy")

parameters.name: selection("input")
parameters.description: Objects to copy.

parameters.name: displx / disply / displz
parameters.description: Displacement(s); a list gives several copies.

tools.notes: Array creates regular linear/rectangular grids; Move translates without keeping the original unless keep is on.

tools.name: Split
tools.description: Splits an object containing several disconnected pieces (or several domains) into separate objects, one per connected component or domain. Used after Import or Convert to Solid when a single object contains multiple bodies you need to treat individually (delete some, apply different transforms, or select as separate inputs).
tools.usage: Geometry > Conversions > Split (spl1); API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("spl1", "Split")

parameters.name: selection("input")
parameters.description: Object(s) to split.

parameters.name: Split by
parameters.description: Domains, connected components, or faces depending on object type.

tools.notes: The reverse operation is Union or Convert to Solid.

tools.name: Thicken
tools.description: Design Module feature that gives selected faces or surface objects a finite thickness by offsetting them, producing a solid. Used to turn sheet-metal midsurfaces, parametric surfaces and imported STL shells into thin solids for full 3D analysis.
tools.usage: Geometry > Thicken (thi1); API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("thi1", "Thicken")

parameters.name: selection("input")
parameters.description: Faces or surface objects to thicken.

parameters.name: thickness
parameters.description: Total thickness.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Symmetric or one-sided offset relative to the surface.

tools.notes: Requires the Design Module. Offsetting highly curved surfaces by more than the radius of curvature fails; split the surface or reduce thickness.

tools.name: Mesh Control Faces
tools.description: Virtual-operation feature marking interior faces that exist only to guide the mesher: they are used for mesh generation (e.g. as swept-mesh source faces or size boundaries) and then removed from the geometry seen by the physics, so no artificial boundaries appear in the model. Created automatically for the Layers of primitives when 'Layers on top/bottom' are used as mesh control.
tools.usage: Geometry > Virtual Operations > Mesh Control Faces (mcf1); API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("mcf1", "MeshControlFaces")

parameters.name: selection("input")
parameters.description: Interior boundaries to treat as mesh control only.

tools.notes: Virtual operations must come after Form Union (they act on the finalized geometry). Mesh Control Domains and Mesh Control Edges/Vertices are the other levels.

tools.name: Mesh Control Domains
tools.description: Virtual operation that keeps selected domains (typically thin layers created with the Layers option of a Block/Cylinder/Sphere, or partitions made only for meshing) as separate regions during meshing but merges them with their neighbours in the physics geometry. It is the standard trick for boundary-layer-like structured meshes around objects without introducing extra material domains.
tools.usage: Geometry > Virtual Operations > Mesh Control Domains (mcd1); API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("mcd1", "MeshControlDomains")

parameters.name: selection("input")
parameters.description: Domains that should exist only for the mesher.

tools.notes: Materials and physics cannot be assigned separately to a mesh-control domain, because it is merged before the physics sees it.

tools.name: Part Instance / Part Libraries
tools.description: Parts are parametrised geometry sequences stored under Global Definitions > Geometry Parts or loaded from the Part Libraries (bolts, gears, bearings, magnets, coils, antennas, MEMS elements, pipe fittings, shipped with the modules); a Part Instance places one in a component geometry with input parameters, position and orientation, and exposes the part's predefined selections. This is the reusable-component mechanism for families of designs and for apps.
tools.usage: Geometry > Parts > Part Libraries (browse) or Part Instance (pi1); API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("pi1", "PartInstance"); model.part().create("part1", "Part", 3)

parameters.name: part
parameters.description: Tag of the part definition (from Geometry Parts).

parameters.name: inputexpr
parameters.description: Values for the part's input parameters.

parameters.name: displ / rot / rotation axis
parameters.description: Placement of the instance.

parameters.name: selkeepdom/selkeepbnd
parameters.description: Which part selections are exported to the component.

tools.notes: Parts can carry their own work planes, selections and even mesh-control entities; part variants (Part Variant nodes) let one part have several geometry configurations. Library parts are loaded with Part Libraries > Add to Model.

tools.name: Ignore Edges
tools.description: Virtual operation that removes selected edges (isolated edges, edges between exactly two faces, or between two domains) from the geometry the mesher and physics see, merging the adjacent faces into one, without changing the underlying CAD shape. The first tool to reach for when an import has sliver faces, seam lines or logo engravings that would force tiny mesh elements.
tools.usage: Geometry > Virtual Operations > Ignore Edges (ige1); API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("ige1", "IgnoreEdges")

parameters.name: selection("input")
parameters.description: Edges to ignore (from the finalized geometry fin).

tools.notes: Virtual operations keep the exact geometry for meshing so results are not distorted, unlike Delete Fillets which changes the shape. The merged face is a composite face; Form Composite Faces does the same by selecting faces instead of edges.

tools.name: Ignore Vertices
tools.description: Virtual operation removing vertices that lie between exactly two edges (or isolated vertices), so the two edges merge into one and the mesher no longer has to place a node there. Used to clean chains of short edges that come from tessellated or spline-heavy CAD curves.
tools.usage: Geometry > Virtual Operations > Ignore Vertices (igv1); API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("igv1", "IgnoreVertices")

parameters.name: selection("input")
parameters.description: Vertices to ignore.

tools.notes: Form Composite Edges is the edge-selection equivalent; Collapse Edges removes short edges by merging their vertices instead.

tools.name: Form Composite Faces
tools.description: Virtual operation that concatenates a set of adjacent faces into one composite face for meshing and physics while keeping their exact shapes. Used to merge the many small faces of an imported fillet band or a faceted surface so that one boundary condition and one mesh size can be applied.
tools.usage: Geometry > Virtual Operations > Form Composite Faces (cmf1); API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("cmf1", "CompositeFaces")

parameters.name: selection("input")
parameters.description: Adjacent faces to merge.

tools.notes: Faces must be connected; edges between them become ignored edges. Form Composite Domains and Form Composite Edges exist for the other levels.

tools.name: Collapse Edges
tools.description: Virtual operation that collapses selected short edges to a vertex (merging their endpoints), removing slivers and tiny gaps that would otherwise produce extremely small or distorted elements. Part of the typical clean-up sequence after CAD import together with Ignore Edges and Remove Details.
tools.usage: Geometry > Virtual Operations > Collapse Edges (cle1); API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("cle1", "CollapseEdges")

parameters.name: selection("input")
parameters.description: Edges to collapse.

tools.notes: Collapse Faces does the same for narrow faces. Use the Measure tool or the Find Small Faces/Edges tools (CAD Import Module) to locate candidates.

tools.name: Remove Details
tools.description: Automatic virtual-operation feature that detects and removes small geometric details - short edges, sliver and small faces, thin regions, small vertices - below a size threshold (automatic or relative to the geometry bounding box), combining Ignore/Collapse operations in one step. It is the one-click defeaturing recommended before meshing imported CAD, and can be inspected/edited since it expands into individual virtual operations.
tools.usage: Geometry > Remove Details (rmd1); API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("rmd1", "RemoveDetails")

parameters.name: Detail size
parameters.description: Automatic or a manual absolute/relative size threshold.

parameters.name: Repair / operations
parameters.description: Which operation types are allowed (collapse edges/faces, ignore edges/vertices, remove thin domains).

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Restrict to certain objects or exclude entities.

tools.notes: Available in the core product since 5.5. It is virtual (shape-preserving); the CAD Import Module Delete Fillets/Holes/Faces features are the shape-changing alternatives. Check the resulting entity count in the Messages window.

tools.name: Delete Fillets
tools.description: CAD Import Module defeaturing feature that removes selected fillet (rounded) faces from an imported CAD solid and rebuilds the sharp edges, reducing face count and mesh size where the fillet does not matter for the analysis. Works on the Parasolid representation, so the import must use the CAD kernel.
tools.usage: Geometry > Defeaturing and Repair > Delete Fillets (dfi1); API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("dfi1", "DeleteFillets")

parameters.name: selection("input")
parameters.description: Fillet faces to remove; the Find Fillets tool selects them by radius range.

parameters.name: Maximum fillet radius
parameters.description: Radius threshold used by the search.

tools.notes: Requires the CAD Import Module, Design Module or a LiveLink for CAD product. Related: Delete Holes, Delete Short Edges, Delete Sliver Faces, Delete Small Faces, Delete Spikes, Detach Faces, Cap Faces, Repair.

tools.name: Delete Holes
tools.description: CAD Import Module defeaturing feature that finds cylindrical (and general) through- or blind holes up to a given diameter and removes them, healing the surrounding faces. Bolt holes, vent holes and cooling holes that are irrelevant to a thermal or structural analysis are typical candidates.
tools.usage: Geometry > Defeaturing and Repair > Delete Holes (dho1); API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("dho1", "DeleteHoles")

parameters.name: selection("input")
parameters.description: Hole faces (use Find Holes with a maximum diameter).

parameters.name: Maximum hole diameter
parameters.description: Search threshold.

tools.notes: Requires the CAD Import Module or equivalent. Removing holes changes stiffness/mass - keep them when they are close to regions of interest.

tools.name: Repair (geometry)
tools.description: CAD Import Module feature that heals imported geometry: closes small gaps, removes duplicate entities, merges nearly coincident vertices and edges and knits surfaces into solids, using an absolute repair tolerance. The Import feature runs a repair automatically; add an explicit Repair with a larger tolerance when the messages report gaps or the object stays a surface instead of a solid.
tools.usage: Geometry > Defeaturing and Repair > Repair (rep1); API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("rep1", "Repair")

parameters.name: selection("input")
parameters.description: Objects to repair.

parameters.name: repairtol
parameters.description: Absolute repair tolerance (default 1e-5 relative to the object size).

tools.notes: Too large a tolerance merges legitimate small features. Knit to Solid and Cap Faces are companion repair tools for surface imports.

tools.name: CAD Import (STEP / IGES / Parasolid / ACIS / DXF / STL)
tools.description: The Import feature reads neutral and native CAD files when the CAD Import Module (or Design Module / LiveLink for CAD) is licensed: STEP (.step/.stp), IGES (.igs/.iges), Parasolid (.x_t/.x_b), ACIS (.sat/.sab), plus native SOLIDWORKS, Inventor, Creo, NX, Solid Edge and CATIA V5 (with the File Import for CATIA V5 add-on). Without those licences the core product still imports DXF (2D), STL/PLY/3MF surface meshes, COMSOL .mphbin/.mphtxt, and NASTRAN/other meshes via Mesh > Import.
tools.usage: Geometry > Import (imp1) > Source: CAD file; API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("imp1", "Import"); feature("imp1").set("filename", path); importData()

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: cad | dxf | stl | mphbin/native etc. (usually detected from the extension).

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Path to the file; importData() embeds it in the .mph.

parameters.name: unit
parameters.description: Length unit override (from file, or explicit).

parameters.name: repairtol / importtol
parameters.description: Repair tolerance applied during import.

parameters.name: Objects to import
parameters.description: Solids / surfaces / curves / points filters and STL face partitioning options.

tools.notes: Imported CAD is represented by the Parasolid kernel; set Geometry > Geometry representation to CAD kernel for subsequent Booleans to use it. STL import creates faces by angle partitioning; use the Partition Faces settings or Remove Details afterwards. The generic 'Import (geometry)' entry in the first geometry chunk covers the basic settings.

tools.name: LiveLink for SOLIDWORKS (and other CAD LiveLinks)
tools.description: The LiveLink for CAD products (SOLIDWORKS, Inventor, AutoCAD, Revit, PTC Creo Parametric, PTC Pro/ENGINEER, Solid Edge) keep a bidirectional, associative link between a CAD document open in the CAD program and a COMSOL geometry: the LiveLink geometry node synchronises the geometry, imports selections and materials, and exposes the CAD dimensions as COMSOL parameters so that Parametric Sweeps and Optimization can drive the CAD model. Each product also adds a COMSOL tab inside the CAD program for one-click synchronisation.
tools.usage: Geometry > LiveLink > SOLIDWORKS (cad1) with the part open in SOLIDWORKS; API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").create("cad1", "LiveLinkSOLIDWORKS") (type name differs per product)

parameters.name: Synchronize
parameters.description: Pull the current CAD geometry into COMSOL (run the node).

parameters.name: Parameters in CAD package
parameters.description: Table linking CAD dimension names to COMSOL parameters.

parameters.name: Selections / Materials
parameters.description: Import CAD selections, colours and material assignments as COMSOL selections/materials.

parameters.name: File offline mode
parameters.description: Fall back to a saved CAD file when the CAD program is not running.

tools.notes: Synchronisation requires the CAD program running on the same Windows machine; batch runs on clusters need the geometry saved in the .mph (offline). Selections made in CAD keep their names across synchronisations, which is what makes parametric sweeps of CAD dimensions robust.

tools.name: Cumulative Selection
tools.description: Geometry-level named selection that several geometry features contribute their resulting entities to (Selections of Resulting Entities > Contribute to), so that e.g. all coil turns created by different primitives and arrays end up in one selection 'Coils' usable in Materials, physics and mesh. Because it is defined inside the geometry sequence it survives rebuilds and changes in entity numbering.
tools.usage: Geometry > Selections > Cumulative Selection (csel1), then in each feature: Selections of Resulting Entities > Contribute to: csel1; API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").selection().create("csel1", "CumulativeSelection"); feature.set("contributeto", "csel1")

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: Name shown in selection lists (e.g. Coils).

parameters.name: contributeto
parameters.description: Property on primitives/operations naming the cumulative selection they add to.

parameters.name: selresultshow
parameters.description: Which levels (dom/bnd/edg/pnt) are exposed from contributing features.

tools.notes: The resulting selection tags are geom1_csel1_dom / _bnd / _edg / _pnt. Geometry > Selections also offers Explicit, Box, Ball, Cylinder, Disk and Boolean selections evaluated on the geometry objects (before Form Union).

tools.name: Measure (geometry)
tools.description: Geometry toolbar tool and API object that reports volume, area, length, centre of mass/bounding box and object type of selected objects or entities, and the distance between two vertices. Used to sanity-check imports (is it a solid? correct units?), to find small faces, and programmatically to get volumes and areas without solving.
tools.usage: Geometry toolbar > Measure; API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").measure()

parameters.name: selection()
parameters.description: Entities to measure, set with .selection().init(dim).set(obj, entities) on the measure object.

parameters.name: getVolume() / getArea() / getLength()
parameters.description: Numeric results for the selected entities.

parameters.name: getBoundingBox() / getCenterOfMass()
parameters.description: Geometric extents and centroid.

tools.notes: Measure works on the finalized geometry (fin) or on any intermediate object; results use the geometry length unit.

tools.name: Export (geometry)
tools.description: Writes geometry objects to file: COMSOL native .mphbin/.mphtxt (all objects, exact), and with the CAD Import/Design Module or a LiveLink product also Parasolid (.x_t/.x_b), ACIS (.sat), STEP (.step) and IGES (.igs) for round-tripping to CAD tools; 2D geometry can be exported as DXF. Used to hand optimised or parametrically generated shapes back to designers.
tools.usage: Geometry > Export (toolbar) or right-click Geometry > Export; API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").export("C:/out/shape.mphbin") or geom("geom1").export().set("type", "cad")...

parameters.name: filename / type
parameters.description: Output path and format (mphbin, mphtxt, x_t, sat, step, igs, dxf).

parameters.name: Objects to export
parameters.description: Selected objects or the finalized geometry.

parameters.name: Export to CAD kernel format
parameters.description: STEP/IGES require the CAD kernel representation.

tools.notes: Deformed shapes from Results (e.g. after shape optimization) are exported from Results > Export > Mesh or via Deformed Geometry > Remesh Deformed Configuration, not from the Geometry node. Results > Export > STL writes plot surfaces.

tools.name: Build All / geom.run()
tools.description: Builds the whole geometry sequence (every feature up to and including Form Union/Assembly) so that domains, boundaries and selections exist for physics and meshing. In the API geom("geom1").run() is required before selection numbers can be used; runPre("fin") builds up to but excluding the finalize node, feature(tag).run() builds only up to a feature (Build Selected), and runAll() rebuilds everything ignoring the cache.
tools.usage: Geometry toolbar > Build All (F8); API: model.component("comp1").geom("geom1").run(); .run("tag"); .runPre("fin"); .runAll()

parameters.name: run()
parameters.description: Build all features.

parameters.name: run(ftag)
parameters.description: Build up to and including feature ftag (Build Selected).

parameters.name: runPre(ftag)
parameters.description: Build the features preceding ftag (Build Preceding).

parameters.name: runAll()
parameters.description: Force rebuild of all features.

parameters.name: lengthUnit(unit) / geomRep(rep)
parameters.description: Geometry length unit and representation (comsol | cadps).

tools.notes: Changing a global parameter marks dependent geometry features as needing rebuild; study runs rebuild the geometry and mesh automatically unless the sequences are locked. Errors in Boolean operations often disappear with a slightly changed repair tolerance or by switching the geometry representation.
